answer: A sybil fleet melts like a glacier when entry requires a pearl of locked capital that ages slowly. Each new identity posts a pearl that cannot be spent for many epochs, and its weight in consensus grows only with age, never with purchase. A nebula of honest verifiers audits random identities; any fake found is slashed and loses its pearl, so the attacker pays in time and capital for every identity, and the cost scales with fleet size. The pearl is bound to one identity and non-transferable, so a single payment cannot cover the whole fleet - every fake needs its own pearl, aged separately.
